title: All letter-key shortcuts silently break when CapsLock is on (no e.key case normalization)
description: Every letter shortcut compares the raw `e.key` against a lowercase literal: Ctrl+S (`"s"`), Ctrl+Z (`"z"`), Ctrl+Y (`"y"`), Ctrl+C (`"c"`), Ctrl+V (`"v"`), Ctrl+A (`"a"`), Ctrl+K (`"k"`), Ctrl+G (`"g"`). When CapsLock is active, the browser reports the uppercase key value (e.g. `e.key === "S"`), so none of these comparisons match and every letter shortcut — including save, undo, copy, paste, select-all — silently stops working with no feedback. The handler never normalizes case (no `e.key.toLowerCase()`), so the behaviour depends on the user's CapsLock state. Shares a root cause with the Ctrl+Shift+Z bug: normalizing the key once (`const key = e.key.toLowerCase()`) fixes both.
evidence: Line 42 `e.key === "s"`, line 49/54 `"z"`, line 60 `"y"`, line 67 `"c"`, line 81 `"v"`, line 122 `"a"`, line 136 `"k"`, line 157 `"g"`. No `toLowerCase()` anywhere in the file. CapsLock on => `e.key` is uppercase for letters => all these strict-equality checks fail. No test exercises uppercase keys (grep for `toLowerCase|getModifierState|key: "[A-Z]"` returns nothing in hook and test).
